_menu_doc: a worker's two build pages (Dominic: civilian and military apart), each in the order its buttons appear (building hotkeys work from either page; hotkeys are avoided where they clash with WASD panning and the debug keys)
_tree_doc: the tech tree page's columns, left to right (scenes/tech_tree.gd); a building missing here goes after these, by age. Buildings with "status": "planned" are drawn on the page as blank frames and skipped by the sim, the build menus and the art bakes (milestone 12)
_walls_doc: "line": placed by dragging a line of tiles (walls); "gate": blocks like a wall but its owner's team walks through it; "length": a gate's footprint is length x size, turned to run along sim x or sim y (chosen at placement, from the wall under it); "replaces": building types of your own it may be dropped on, taking their place (a gate into a wall line)
_age_looks_doc: per architecture and building type, the model it takes from an age on, e.g. {"junk": {"town_center": {"3": "concept_junk_tc_pride"}}}: a culture's buildings grow with the ages. Empty until Dominic picks (concept rounds RB3 and on)
_workers_doc: "workers": how many workers may work a building's ground at once (Dominic: one farmer per farm, as in the genre); others sent to it go to a farm nobody works, else other food nearby, else wait by it. Left out: no limit
_idle_note_doc: "idle_note": a line the command panel shows for a finished building with nothing to train or research (the Siege Workshop before its engines)
_scale_doc: a culture's own size for a building type (Dominic: the rats' house and barracks, smaller, D-090)
_garrison_doc: units shelter inside a building type with "garrison": N (src/sim/garrison.gd): up to N of its owner's units (none with a tag in garrison.not, e.g. riders and giants; workers always fit, centaurs' too), hidden, healed 1 hp every heal_every ticks, seeing nothing beyond the building. A building with an "attack" shoots attack.arrows arrows a volley (towers 1; 0: the Town Center only shoots with people inside) plus one per unit inside. Destroyed, it spills them out. The Town Center's call to arms sends its owner's workers within call_range tiles into the nearest building with room. "sight": the building's own sight radius in tiles (else the rules' fog.tower for buildings that shoot, fog.building for the rest). "more_from_age": a player who already has one may build another only from that age on (Town Centers, age 3). "upgrade_of": a building that research turns another into, in place ({"building": "watchtower", "becomes": "bastion"} in tech.json); once researched, ordering the old one builds the new
_variants_doc: how many looks a type bakes (turned a quarter round, nudged in size); each building picks one, like rocks

archery_range.name: Archery Range
archery_range.desc: Trains your ranged soldiers: skirmishers, who hunt archers, and archers.

armoury.name: Armoury
armoury.desc: Where weapons and armour are improved: sharper points, better bows, tougher kit.
armoury.note: weapon and armour research (Sharp Sticks moved here, Dominic)

barracks.name: Barracks
barracks.desc: Trains your foot soldiers: spearmen, who hold against riders and big beasts, and swordsmen, who cut through spearmen and skirmishers and break buildings.
barracks.note: infantry (the spear and swordsman lines); the Archery Range and Stable train the rest

farm.name: Farm
farm.desc: A field of food that workers tend without walking far. When it's worked out it lies fallow; reseed it for wood.
farm.note: when built, its ground becomes crops (a rice paddy in water, for amphibians): one farm, one pool of food; worked out it lies fallow, and a worker can reseed it for wood

house.name: House
house.desc: Room for more of your people. Every unit needs space; without houses, training stops.

pen.name: Pen
pen.desc: A fold for your herd animals. Penned, they give a little food all the time and breed, instead of a lot of food once. Right-click it with sheep selected to put them in.
pen.note: walked into once built (animals stand inside it); each penned herd animal, up to pen.animals, adds pen.food food every pen.food_every seconds with no worker (a 100-food sheep pays back in about 7 minutes and keeps going); with two or more inside, a new one is born every pen.breed_every seconds up to the cap. Torn down, its animals spill out (the steal rule applies again)

lumber_camp.name: Lumber Camp
lumber_camp.desc: A place to drop wood close to where it's cut. Woodcutting research is done here.

market.name: Market
market.desc: Buy and sell food, wood and stone for gold. Prices move with what everyone trades.
market.note: trade: buy/sell with gold, shared prices

mill.name: Mill
mill.desc: A place to drop food near bushes and farms. Foraging and farming research is done here.

mining_camp.name: Mining Camp
mining_camp.desc: A place to drop stone and gold close to the deposits. Mining research is done here.

stable.name: Stable
stable.desc: Trains your large unit: a rider, a giant or a heavy, whatever your race fields.
stable.note: the large unit (mounts, giants or heavies)

town_center.name: Town Center
town_center.desc: The heart of your town: trains workers, takes in every resource, and is where you age up. People inside shoot from it. Lose every one and you lose.
town_center.note: every player starts with one (free); more from age 3, for wood and stone; shoots one arrow per unit inside

wall.name: Stone Wall
wall.desc: A stone wall, one tile at a time: drag to lay a line. Stops anyone who can't fly; put a Stone Gate in it to let your own side through.
wall.note: dragged in lines; flyers go over

watchtower.name: Watchtower
watchtower.desc: A lookout that shoots the nearest enemy in range and sees far into the fog. Each unit inside adds an arrow.
watchtower.note: shoots the nearest enemy in range

palisade.name: Palisade Wall
palisade.desc: A wall of sharpened stakes, one tile at a time: drag to lay a line. Cheap and quick, but it won't hold for long. Flyers go over.
palisade.note: dragged in lines; the age-1 wall

palisade_gate.name: Palisade Gate
palisade_gate.desc: A stake gate three tiles long: drop it on your palisade and it follows the line (on open ground, R turns it). It opens for your side and stays shut to everyone else.

stone_gate.name: Stone Gate
stone_gate.desc: A stone gatehouse three tiles long: drop it on your stone wall and it follows the line (on open ground, R turns it). It opens for your side and stays shut to everyone else.

outpost.name: Outpost
outpost.desc: A cheap lookout post: it sees far into the fog, but it doesn't shoot and nobody fits inside.
outpost.note: sight only: no attack, no garrison

siege_workshop.name: Siege Workshop
siege_workshop.desc: A yard of timber frames where siege engines are built: rams for gates and walls, catapults for towers and crowds, bolt throwers for lines of soldiers.
siege_workshop.note: trains the siege lines (milestone 13); the siege tower is milestone 16's

university.name: University
university.desc: Research for buildings, towers and siege: stronger walls, taller towers, longer reach.
university.note: building, tower, wall and siege research (milestone 12 phase 4)

castle.name: Castle
castle.desc: A stone fortress that looses a volley of arrows at every enemy in reach and shelters your soldiers. Its own research: War Drums and your race's two tricks.
castle.note: shoots `arrows` arrows a volley, each at the next-nearest foe (src/sim/combat.gd _towers); garrison: how many units shelter inside (the garrison system, milestone 12 phase 3); trains nothing yet (unique unit, sapper and great sling are milestone 13)

wonder.name: Wonder
wonder.desc: A great work of your people. Build it and keep it standing long enough, and your side wins. Everyone sees the countdown.
wonder.note: alternative victory (src/sim/match.gd, host rule "wonder"): finished and standing for rules.wonder.hold_seconds, its owner's team wins

bastion.name: Bastion
bastion.desc: A stone tower, taller and tougher than a watchtower: it hits harder and further. Each unit inside adds an arrow.
bastion.note: what the Bastion research at the University makes of every Watchtower (in place, keeping its share of health); after it, ordering a Watchtower builds a Bastion
